meta.title: Bioprinting of stem cell expansion lattices.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Alginate lattices were printed with neural progenitor cells to expand them in 3D for cell manufacturing. Alginate stiffness (30 Pa to 1 kPa) changed how well the cells expanded.

formulations.crosslinking: CaSO4 pre-crosslink, printed into gelatin/CaCl2 support
formulations.stiffness_note: G' ~1 kPa (stiffest); 0.1 kPa intermediate; 0.03 kPa softest
formulations.name: 2% alginate, 8 mM Ca2+ (stem cell expansion lattice)
formulations.composition_detail: 2% w/v alginate (LVG/VLVG blends) pre-crosslinked with 8 mM Ca2+; RGD variant
formulations.key_outcome: Printed alginate lattices allowed 3D expansion of NPCs for biomanufacturing, with stiffness affecting growth.

evidence.quote: Alginate bioinks (8 mM Ca2+, 30 ×106 NPCs/mL, 2% w/v) were extruded through a 22-gauge needle
with the stiffest gels (plateau storage shear modulus, G′ ~ 1 kPa) using a large molecular weight alginate
